releases.legal_basis: Informed Patient consent to permit the receipt, processing and release of data by the HSCIC

texts.e11eae37a023: Objective for processing: The primary objective of the study is to compare the cardiovascular safety of celecoxib and traditional Non-Steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs via a randomised Clinical Trial (NSAIDs). The secondary objective of the study is to compare the gastrointestinal safety of celecoxib and traditional NSAIDs. The present proposal seeks to compare the cardiovascular and gastrointestinal safety and effectiveness of a strategy of initial randomisation to treatment with the selective COX-2 inhibitor celecoxib or to ‘usual care’ with their current non-selective NSAID therapy (with or without cyto-protection with ulcer healing drug use in either celecoxib or ‘usual care’ limbs) but now want to link this data with HES Admitted Patient Care data with the ONS data received under MR1305 as they require access to details of all hospitalisations, deaths and diagnoses of cancer within their study population (cohort). There for the main objective is to fulfill a European Medicines Agency request to establish the comparative safety of Non-Steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs via a randomised Clinical Trial (NSAID) prescribed for the treatment of arthritis. Processing activities: The data will be used to establish and confirm any hospitalisations, deaths and serious adverse events which have occurred for patients participating in the SCOT Study. As such it will be reviewed by approved study personnel and further information gathered as necessary to complete the reporting of information on the events within the study database. Serious adverse events will be listed and summarized in the statistical analysis Specific outputs expected, including target date: Study results will be presented at the European Society of Cardiology in September 2015, and published in peer reviewed academic journals such as Lancet and New England Journal of Medicines. This is expected in late 2015. No identifiable or record level data will be disclosed to third parties. The data derived from record linkage will only be shared between the Sponsor (University of Dundee), it’s data management team (Robertson Centre, University of Glasgow who are the data processes who are subcontracted by the University of Dundee to deal with the data management and deal with the analysis and return analysis back to Dundee which is stripped of identifiers), and academic collaborators within England/Scotland (local universities employ local research nurses) who would use the de-identified data to get hold of patient medical records, so that an independent committee of physicians (who will only see patient medical notes stripped of personal information) could adjudicate on the relationship between the hospitalisation/death/cancer and their randomised therapy in our drug trial. All of those parties are subject to data sharing/privacy agreements, and will not disclose the information to any external party, except where warranted under law. Expected measurable benefits to health and/or social care including target date: NSAIDs are commonly used medications. Traditional NSAIDs are associated with significant morbidity and mortality from gastrointestinal toxicity. Cyclooxygenase 2 (COX-2) selective agents are associated with reduced upper gastrointestinal toxicity. Traditional NSAIDs and COX-2 inhibitors may also be associated with cardiovascular toxicity. However, the overall safety balance of a strategy of celecoxib therapy versus a strategy of NSAID therapy is unknown. The European Medicines Agency (EMA) requested that studies of the cardiovascular safety of celecoxib be carried out within the indicated population in Europe. This study addresses these issues by comparing the cardiovascular safety of celecoxib therapy with traditional NSAID therapy in the setting of the EU healthcare system. Results are expected to be presented on 02/09/2015 at the European Society of Cardiology who will present the results of the analysis face to face; the analysis will be high level statistics.
